explanation.text:
(Lam. 3:1-66)

seen affliction--his own in the dungeon of Malchiah (Jer 38:6); that of his countrymen also in the siege. Both were types of that of Christ.

bsb.text: I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of God’s wrath.

explanation.text:
darkness--calamity.

light--prosperity.

bsb.text: He has driven me away and made me walk in darkness instead of light.

explanation.text: turneth . . . hand--to inflict again and again new strokes. "His hand," which once used to protect me. "Turned . . . turneth" implies repeated inflictions.

bsb.text: Indeed, He keeps turning His hand against me all day long.
He has worn away my flesh and skin; He has shattered my bones.

explanation.text: builded--mounds, as against a besieged city, so as to allow none to escape (so Lam 3:7, Lam 3:9).

bsb.text: He has besieged me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.

explanation.text:
set me--HENDERSON refers this to the custom of placing the dead in a sitting posture.

dark places--sepulchers. As those "dead long since"; so Jeremiah and his people are consigned to oblivion (Psa 88:5-6; Psa 143:3; Eze 37:13).

bsb.text: He has made me dwell in darkness like those dead for ages.

explanation.text:
hedged-- (Job 3:23; Hos 2:6).

chain--literally, "chain of brass."

bsb.text: He has walled me in so I cannot escape; He has weighed me down with chains.

explanation.text: shutteth out--image from a door shutting out any entrance (Job 30:20). So the antitype. Christ (Psa 22:2).

bsb.text: Even when I cry out and plead for help, He shuts out my prayer.

explanation.text:
hewn stone--which coheres so closely as not to admit of being broken through.

paths crooked--thwarted our plans and efforts so that none went right.

bsb.text: He has barred my ways with cut stones; He has made my paths crooked.
He is a bear lying in wait, a lion hiding in ambush.

explanation.text:
turned aside--made me wander out of the right way, so as to become a prey to wild beasts.

pulled in pieces-- (Hos 6:1), as a "bear" or a "lion" (Lam 3:10).

bsb.text: He forced me off my path and tore me to pieces; He left me without help.
He bent His bow and set me as the target for His arrow.

explanation.text: arrows--literally, "sons" of His quiver (compare Job 6:4).

bsb.text: He pierced my kidneys with His arrows.

explanation.text:
(Jer 20:7).

their song-- (Psa 69:12). Jeremiah herein was a type of Messiah. "All my people" (Joh 1:11).

bsb.text: I am a laughingstock to all my people; they mock me in song all day long.

explanation.text: wormwood-- (Jer 9:15). There it is regarded as food, namely, the leaves: here as drink, namely, the juice.

bsb.text: He has filled me with bitterness; He has intoxicated me with wormwood.

explanation.text: gravel--referring to the grit that often mixes with bread baked in ashes, as is the custom of baking in the East (Pro 20:17). We fare as hardly as those who eat such bread. The same allusion is in "Covered me with ashes," namely, as bread.

bsb.text: He has ground my teeth with gravel and trampled me in the dust.

explanation.text: Not only present, but all hope of future prosperity is removed; so much so, that I am as one who never was prosperous ("I forgat prosperity").

bsb.text: My soul has been deprived of peace; I have forgotten what prosperity is.

explanation.text: from the Lord--that is, my hope derived from Him (Psa 31:22).

bsb.text: So I say, “My strength has perished, along with my hope from the LORD.”

explanation.text:
This gives the reason why he gave way to the temptation to despair. The Margin, "Remember" does not suit the sense so well.

wormwood . . . gall-- (Jer 9:15).

bsb.text: Remember my affliction and wandering, the wormwood and the gall.

explanation.text: As often as my soul calls them to remembrance, it is humbled or bowed down in me.

bsb.text: Surely my soul remembers and is humbled within me.

explanation.text: This--namely, what follows; the view of the divine character (Lam 3:22-23). CALVIN makes "this" refer to Jeremiah's infirmity. His very weakness (Lam 3:19-20) gives him hope of God interposing His strength for him (compare Psa 25:11, Psa 25:17; Psa 42:5, Psa 42:8; Co2 12:9-10).

bsb.text: Yet I call this to mind, and therefore I have hope:
Because of the loving devotion of the LORD we are not consumed, for His mercies never fail.
They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness!

explanation.text: (Num 18:20; Psa 16:5; Psa 73:26; Psa 119:57; Jer 10:16). To have God for our portion is the one only foundation of hope.

bsb.text: “The LORD is my portion,” says my soul, “therefore I will hope in Him.”

explanation.text:
The repetition of "good" at the beginning of each of the three verses heightens the effect.

wait-- (Isa 30:18).

bsb.text: The LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul who seeks Him.

explanation.text: quietly wait--literally, "be in silence." Compare Lam 3:28 and Psa 39:2, Psa 39:9, that is, to be patiently quiet under afflictions, resting in the will of God (Psa 37:7). So Aaron (Lev 10:2-3); and Job (Job 40:4-5).

bsb.text: It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the LORD.

explanation.text: yoke--of the Lord's disciplinary teaching (Psa 90:12; Psa 119:71). CALVIN interprets it, The Lord's doctrine (Mat 11:29-30), which is to be received in a docile spirit. The earlier the better; for the old are full of prejudices (Pro 8:17; Ecc 12:1). Jeremiah himself received the yoke, both of doctrine and chastisement in his youth (Jer 1:6-7).

bsb.text: It is good for a man to bear the yoke while he is still young.

explanation.text:
The fruit of true docility and patience. He does not fight against the yoke (Jer 31:18; Act 9:5), but accommodates himself to it.

alone--The heathen applauded magnanimity, but they looked to display and the praise of men. The child of God, in the absence of any witness, "alone," silently submits to the will of God.

borne it upon him--that is, because he is used to bearing it on him. Rather, "because He (the Lord, Lam 3:26) hath laid it on him" [VATABLUS].

bsb.text: Let him sit alone in silence, for the LORD has laid it upon him.

explanation.text:
(Job 42:6). The mouth in the dust is the attitude of suppliant and humble submission to God's dealings as righteous and loving in design (compare Ezr 9:6; Co1 14:25).

if so be there may be hope--This does not express doubt as to whether GOD be willing to receive the penitent, but the penitent's doubt as to himself; he whispers to himself this consolation, "Perhaps there may be hope for me."

bsb.text: Let him bury his face in the dust—perhaps there is still hope.

explanation.text: Messiah, the Antitype, fulfilled this; His practice agreeing with His precept (Isa 50:6; Mat 5:39). Many take patiently afflictions from God, but when man wrongs them, they take it impatiently. The godly bear resignedly the latter, like the former, as sent by God (Psa 17:13).

bsb.text: Let him offer his cheek to the one who would strike him; let him be filled with reproach.

explanation.text: True repentance is never without hope (Psa 94:14).

bsb.text: For the Lord will not cast us off forever.

explanation.text: The punishments of the godly are but for a time.

bsb.text: Even if He causes grief, He will show compassion according to His abundant loving devotion.

explanation.text: He does not afflict any willingly (literally, "from His heart," that is, as if He had any pleasure in it, Eze 33:11), much less the godly (Heb 12:10).

bsb.text: For He does not willingly afflict or grieve the sons of men.

explanation.text: This triplet has an infinitive in the beginning of each verse, the governing finite verb being in the end of Lam 3:36, "the Lord approveth not," which is to be repeated in each verse. Jeremiah here anticipates and answers the objections which the Jews might start, that it was by His connivance they were "crushed under the feet" of those who "turned aside the right of a man." God approves (literally, "seeth," Hab 1:13; so "behold," "look on," that is, look on with approval) not of such unrighteous acts; and so the Jews may look for deliverance and the punishment of their foes.

bsb.text: To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the land,

explanation.text: before . . . face of . . . most High--Any "turning aside" of justice in court is done before the face of God, who Is present, and "regardeth," though unseen (Ecc 5:8).

bsb.text: to deny a man justice before the Most High,

explanation.text: subvert--to wrong.

bsb.text: to subvert a man in his lawsuit—of these the Lord does not approve.

explanation.text: Who is it that can (as God, Psa 33:9) effect by a word anything, without the will of God?

bsb.text: Who has spoken and it came to pass, unless the Lord has ordained it?

explanation.text: evil . . . good--Calamity and prosperity alike proceed from God (Job 2:10; Isa 45:7; Amo 3:6).

bsb.text: Do not both adversity and good come from the mouth of the Most High?

explanation.text:
living--and so having a time yet given him by God for repentance. If sin were punished as it deserves, life itself would be forfeited by the sinner. "Complaining" (murmuring) ill becomes him who enjoys such a favor as life (Pro 19:3).

for the punishment of his sins--Instead of blaming God for his sufferings, he ought to recognize in them God's righteousness and the just rewards of his own sin.

bsb.text: Why should any mortal man complain, in view of his sins?

explanation.text:
us--Jeremiah and his fellow countrymen in their calamity.

search--as opposed to the torpor wherewith men rest only on their outward sufferings, without attending to the cause of them (Psa 139:23-24).

bsb.text: Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the LORD.

explanation.text: heart with . . . hands--the antidote to hypocrisy (Psa 86:4; Ti1 2:8).

bsb.text: Let us lift up our hearts and hands to God in heaven:

explanation.text: not pardoned--The Babylonian captivity had not yet ended.

bsb.text: “We have sinned and rebelled; You have not forgiven.”

explanation.text: covered--namely, thyself (so Lam 3:44), so as not to see and pity our calamities, for even the most cruel in seeing a sad spectacle are moved to pity. Compare as to God "hiding His face," Psa 10:11; Psa 22:25.

bsb.text: You have covered Yourself in anger and pursued us; You have killed without pity.

explanation.text: (Lam 3:8). The "cloud" is our sins, and God's wrath because of them (Isa 44:22; Isa 59:2).

bsb.text: You have covered Yourself with a cloud that no prayer can pass through.

explanation.text: So the apostles were treated; but, instead of murmuring, they rejoiced at it (Co1 4:13).

bsb.text: You have made us scum and refuse among the nations.

explanation.text: Pe is put before Ain (Lam 3:43, Lam 3:46), as in Lam 2:16-17; Lam 4:16-17. (Lam 2:16.)

bsb.text: All our enemies open their mouths against us.

explanation.text: Like animals fleeing in fear, we fall into the snare laid for us.

bsb.text: Panic and pitfall have come upon us—devastation and destruction.
Streams of tears flow from my eyes over the destruction of the daughter of my people.

explanation.text: without . . . intermission--or else, "because there is no intermission" [PISCATOR], namely, Of my miseries.

bsb.text: My eyes overflow unceasingly, without relief,

explanation.text:
Till--His prayer is not without hope, wherein it differs from the blind grief of unbelievers.

look down, etc.-- (Isa 63:15).

bsb.text: until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.

explanation.text:
eye affecteth mine heart--that is, causeth me grief with continual tears; or, "affecteth my life" (literally, "soul," Margin), that is, my health [GROTIUS].

daughters of . . . city--the towns around, dependencies of Jerusalem, taken by the foe.

bsb.text: My eyes bring grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.

explanation.text:
a bird--which is destitute of counsel and strength. The allusion seems to be to Pro 1:17 [CALVIN].

without cause-- (Psa 69:4; Psa 109:3-4). Type of Messiah (Joh 15:25).

bsb.text: Without cause my enemies hunted me like a bird.

explanation.text:
in . . . dungeon-- (Jer 37:16).

stone--usually put at the mouth of a dungeon to secure the prisoners (Jos 10:18; Dan 6:17; Mat 27:60).

bsb.text: They dropped me alive into a pit and cast stones upon me.

explanation.text:
Waters--not literally, for there was "no water" (Jer 38:6) in the place of Jeremiah's confinement, but emblematical of overwhelming calamities (Psa 69:2; Psa 124:4-5).

cut off-- (Isa 38:10-11). I am abandoned by God. He speaks according to carnal sense.

bsb.text: The waters flowed over my head, and I thought I was going to die.

explanation.text: I called out of dungeon--Thus the spirit resists the flesh, and faith spurns the temptation [CALVIN], (Psa 130:1; Jon 2:2).

bsb.text: I called on Your name, O LORD, out of the depths of the Pit.

explanation.text:
Thou hast heard--namely formerly (so in Lam 3:57-58).

breathing . . . cry--two kinds of prayer; the sigh of a prayer silently breathed forth, and the loud, earnest cry (compare "prayer," "secret speech," Isa 26:16, Margin; with "cry aloud," Psa 55:17).

bsb.text: You heard my plea: “Do not ignore my cry for relief.”

explanation.text: Thou drewest near--with Thy help (Jam 4:8).

bsb.text: You drew near when I called on You; You said, “Do not be afraid.”

explanation.text:
Jeremiah cites God's gracious answers to his prayers as an encouragement to his fellow countrymen, to trust in Him.

pleaded-- (Psa 35:1; Mic 7:9).

bsb.text: You defend my cause, O Lord; You redeem my life.

explanation.text: God's past deliverances and His knowledge of Judah's wrongs are made the grounds of prayer for relief.

bsb.text: You have seen, O LORD, the wrong done to me; vindicate my cause!

explanation.text:
imaginations--devices (Jer 11:19).

Their vengeance--means their malice. Jeremiah gives his conduct, when plotted against by his foes, as an example how the Jews should bring their wrongs at the hands of the Chaldeans before God.

bsb.text: You have seen all their malice, all their plots against me.

explanation.text: their reproach--their reproachful language against me.

bsb.text: O LORD, You have heard their insults, all their plots against me—

explanation.text: lips--speeches.

bsb.text: the slander and murmuring of my assailants against me all day long.

explanation.text: sitting down . . . rising up--whether they sit or rise, that is, whether they be actively engaged or sedentary, and at rest "all the day" (Lam 3:62), I am the subject of their derisive songs (Lam 3:14).

bsb.text: When they sit and when they rise, see how they mock me in song.
You will pay them back what they deserve, O LORD, according to the work of their hands.

explanation.text: sorrow--rather, blindness or hardness; literally, "a veil" covering their heart, so that they may rush on to their own ruin (Isa 6:10; Co2 3:14-15).

bsb.text: Put a veil of anguish over their hearts; may Your curse be upon them!

explanation.text:
from under . . . heavens of . . . Lord--destroy them so that it may be seen everywhere under heaven that thou sittest above as Judge of the world.

Next: Lamentations Chapter 4

bsb.text: You will pursue them in anger and exterminate them from under Your heavens, O LORD.
